narr: A deep stream of moisture was pulled northwestward from the Atlantic Ocean into the mountains of south-central Pennsylvania around an upper level low centered over the Ohio Valley during the afternoon and evening hours of May 13. 2025. This led to extensive flooding and flash flooding across Somerset County and southwestern Bedford County, and more sporadic flooding from the remainder of Bedford County eastward into Fulton and Franklin counties.
ev: Flash flooding partially submerged a car in 2 to 3 feet on McKenzie Hollow Road near Tall Pine Drive and Fallen Oak Drive, requiring a water rescue.
Flash flooding led to the evacuation of low-lying areas in and around Meyersdale.
Flash flooding stranded a car in rapidly rising water in the 7000 block of Mount Davis Road near Meyersdale near the fairgrounds, resulting in one injury.
Flash flooding led to a water rescue on the 700 block of Engles Mill Road east of Salisbury.

Flash flooding led to a swift water rescue in Boynton when an occupied vehicle went into Little Piney Creek at the Route 219 bridge and Post Office Street and floated downstream into the Cassleman River. Rescue operations were set up at the Coal Run Road bridge in Boynton.
Flash-flooding led to the evacuation of low-lying areas in and around Salisbury.
Flash flooding led to an occupied vehicle becoming stranded in approximately 3 feet of water, requiring a water rescue.
Flash flooding occurred along Gooseberry Road near Hyndman, with up to 4 feet of water across the roadway.
